title: Egress proxy connection-pools & TCP session smoothing - TF sketch
content:
Purpose and scope

This is a working sketch for an on-prem/VPC egress proxy module and operational playbook focused on connection pooling, TCP session smoothing, and the Terraform interface for customers using Redwood Private. The goal: reduce ephemeral port exhaustion and TLS handshake pressure during bursty inference traffic while keeping latency SLOs intact. This doc captures design constraints, tf module surface, upgrade steps, test plans, and observability signals.

Context / motivation

We repeatedly see two correlated failure modes for private deployments running inference at scale behind customer NATs: (1) ephemeral port pressure on the customer egress path during bursty traffic patterns (model hot loops, autoscale spikes), and (2) high CPU/latency due to repeated TLS handshakes when short-lived upstream connections are opened for every request. Traditional NAT affinity solutions help but are brittle when pods scale or k8s service IPs rotate. A local egress proxy that reuses long-lived upstream connections (pooling) and smooths TCP session behavior reduces both problems without requiring changes to customer network policies.

High-level approach

- Deploy a small, horizontally-scaled egress-proxy tier (Envoy/HAProxy flavor) as DaemonSet or Deployment in the private cluster.
- Proxy performs connection pooling to upstream model endpoints (hosted/dedicated) and uses keepalives and TLS session resumption to reduce handshake CPU.
- Proxy exposes a TCP-level pooling config and an HTTP-layer idle/ageing policy; proxy maintains affinity buckets keyed by model+region+cert-fingerprint.
- Terraform module provides: (a) proxy deployment + config map templates, (b) service + NodePort/HostNetwork options, (c) optional NAT/egress-route infra (Cloud NAT resources for GCP customers), (d) RBAC and PSP/PodSecurity requirements, (e) Prometheus scrape annotations and grafana-folder scaffolding.

Key design constraints and tradeoffs

- Latency SLO: pooling must not add head-of-line blocking for low-QPS, low-latency requests. Keep a small pool-per-target per-proxy (e.g., 2-8) with connection borrowing/backpressure.
- Pool scaling: avoid unbounded per-target connection growth. Implement configurable max_conns_per_target and per-proxy global_max_conns.
- TLS complexity: enable session resumption (TLS tickets) and TLS 1.3 0-RTT where supported; but fall back to full handshake if upstream doesn't support it. Consider CPU tradeoffs with 0-RTT replay safety.
- Failure modes: upstream misbehaving (slow responses) should not stall the pool; use circuit-breakers and short hedged requests for tail latency cases.
- Customer transparency: keep NAT source IP behavior predictable; document that egress will be proxied from the proxy node IPs.

Terraform module surface (sketch)

Module name: redwood_private/egress_proxy
Inputs (subset):
- name_prefix (string)
- namespace (string)
- proxy_image (string, default: redwood/egress-proxy:canary)
- mode (string enum: "daemonset" | "deployment")
- host_network (bool)
- service_type (string enum: "ClusterIP" | "NodePort" )
- upstream_targets (list<string>) -- canonical upstream hostnames or target groups
- pool_max_per_target (number, default 6)
- pool_min_per_target (number, default 2)
- global_max_conns (number, default 1024)
- idle_connection_timeout_seconds (number, default 60)
- tls_resume_policy (string enum: "auto" | "disabled" | "require")
- enable_tls_0rtt (bool, default false)
- healthcheck_path (string)
- prometheus_annotations (map)
- node_selector (map)
- tolerations (list)
- rbac_enabled (bool, default true)

Outputs (sketch):
- service_name
- configmap_name
- deployment_name
- grafana_dashboard_id (if managed)

Notes: keep the tf interface deliberately small; advanced tuning lives in the ConfigMap applied by platform teams. Module should optionally emit a k8s Job that runs a post-deploy validation script (see verification below).

Recommended proxy runtime knobs (defaults with rationale)

- pool_min_per_target: 2 (ensures immediate reuse, avoids cold open for small QPS)
- pool_max_per_target: 6 (caps growth, empirical balance for 95th tail)
- global_max_conns: 1024 (warn if cluster nodes have small ephemeral port ranges)
- idle_connection_timeout_seconds: 60 (release truly idle upstreams while preserving session resumption windows)
- tcp_keepalive_interval: 30s; tcp_keepalive_probes: 3 (helps NAT keepalive)
- connection_borrow_timeout_ms: 100 (fast error for backpressure instead of head-of-line wait)

Operational playbook: rollout and upgrade plan

Phased rollout (targeting a single customer cluster):
1) Canary deploy (mode=daemonset) to 1 node pool, read-only traffic: traffic mirroring from app frontend to proxy for 24–48 hours. Observe connection counts, handshake rate, CPU.
2) Small scale pilot: accept 5% egress traffic through proxy (routing via local iptables redirect or sidecar) for 72 hours. Run load generator reproducing typical inference bursts.
3) Ramp to 25% after quality gates pass (latency p50/p95, CPU, no increase in TCP resets).
4) Full cutover with circuit-breaker rules to fall back to direct egress if proxy overload detected.

Upgrade steps (minor version changes):
- Preflight: run terraform plan and diff of ConfigMap changes. Validate new config doesn't reduce pool sizes below safe thresholds.
- Drain: scale down proxy pods with rolling update, verify upstream connections drop gradually, monitor ephemeral port usage.
- Rollout: 25% rolling replacement with health-probes (http 200 on /_ready) and Prometheus checks for tcp_reuse_ratio.
- Post-check: run smoke tests and traffic replay for 1 hour, ensure no TLS handshake CPU spike and no >1% request error increase.

Hardening and kernel/sysctl guidance (customer facing suggestions)

- Increase ephemeral port range if customers report port exhaustion: net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range = 15000 61000
- Reduce TIME_WAIT retention for long-lived proxies: net.ipv4.tcp_fin_timeout = 30
- Enable TCP Tw Reuse where safe: net.ipv4.tcp_tw_reuse = 1 (note: only if NAT behavior understood)
- Tune netfilter conntrack for high connection churn: net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max tuned based on expected concurrent flows

Testing and validation checklist

Pre-deploy tests (CI):
- Unit tests for terraform module input validation
- K8s apply dry-run with schema validation
- Linting for ConfigMap templates

Canary tests:
- Load test: burst pattern (10k qps bursts for 30s every 5m) against mirrored traffic
- Ephemeral port simulation: measure source port reuse rate across cluster nodes
- TLS handshake measurement: handshakes/sec before and after proxy
- Failure injection: circuit-break upstream (500/timeout) and observe proxy backoff/circuit-break behavior

Post-deploy smoke:
- Verify p95 latency remains within 1.2x baseline
- No increase in connection_reset_count metric > 0.5% of total requests

Observability: metrics and alerts

Instrument the proxy to emit:
- upstream_conn_count_total (gauge per upstream)
- upstream_conn_in_use (gauge)
- tcp_reuse_ratio (gauge derived: reused_conns / total_conns)
- tls_handshakes_per_minute
- tls_session_resume_ratio
- conn_borrow_time_ms_p50/p95
- conn_fail_rate (rate of borrow failures)
- circuit_break_count

Suggested alerts (examples):
- High ephemeral port pressure: host_ephemeral_port_free < 1500 -> P2 alert to infra team
- TLS handshake surge: increase > 3x baseline for 5m -> P3 investigate suspect config or upstream changes
- Borrow failure rate > 1% for 10m -> degrade routing to direct egress and page SRE

Known risks and mitigation

- Increased blast radius if proxy misconfigures upstream routing (mitigate by conservative canary and circuit breakers).
- Incorrect assumptions about customer firewall/NAT policies (document and require a simple preflight network test that verifies outbound IPs and path MTU).
- TLS 0-RTT replay risk — disable by default unless customer explicitly opts in and understands replay semantics.

Open design decisions (to decide in next sprint)

- Centralized vs node-local pools: node-local reduces cross-node traffic and preserves source IP but consumes more upstream connections overall. Need cost analysis.
- Persistent TLS tickets: should the proxy persist TLS session tickets to disk (improves reuse after restarts) vs in-memory only (safer for ephemeral).
- Integrate with Redwood routing rules to prefer cheaper model variant endpoints under load — impact on pool keys and pooling efficiency needs study.

Appendix: example Envoy snippets (conceptual)

- cluster config: circuit_breakers: max_connections: {{pool_max_per_target}}
- connection_pool: tcp_connection_pool: { idle_timeout: {{idle_connection_timeout_seconds}}s, max_requests: 0 }
- upstream transport_socket: tls_context: { enable_session_resumption: true }

Next steps / action items

- Finalize terraform module inputs (Alyssa) by 2024-12-01
- PM/SE validation checklist: Devika to draft customer preflight test steps by 2024-12-05
- Run initial canary in staging with load generator (Ethan) week of 2024-12-09

Notes to reviewers

This is intentionally a sketch: anticipating multiple iterations as we collect telemetry from pilot clusters. Please leave feedback inline (especially on the tf surface and default pool sizing). If you have prior art from customer deployments where proxy pooling harmed tail latency, call it out and we will add hedging/early-fail strategies.

---
